subject: General Knowledge
topic: Famous temples of India — mixed tiers

questions.stem: The Dilwara Temples, celebrated for their exquisite white marble craftsmanship, are located at Mount Abu in which Indian state?

options.option_text: Rajasthan, in the Aravalli hill range
Gujarat, near the border with Rajasthan
Madhya Pradesh, in the Vindhya hill range
Maharashtra, in the northern Western Ghats

questions.explanation: The Dilwara Temples are a group of five Jain temples built between the 11th–16th centuries CE at Mount Abu, the only hill station in Rajasthan, situated in the Aravalli range. Option B (Gujarat) is a classic confusion because Mount Abu lies very close to the Rajasthan–Gujarat border, but administratively it belongs to Rajasthan's Sirohi district.

questions.stem: The Kashi Vishwanath Temple — one of the twelve Jyotirlingas — is situated on the western bank of which sacred river?

options.option_text: River Yamuna, flowing through Agra and Delhi
River Godavari, revered as the Ganga of the South
River Ganga, flowing through the city of Varanasi
River Narmada, flowing westward through Madhya Pradesh

questions.explanation: Kashi Vishwanath Temple stands on the western bank of the Ganga in Varanasi (Kashi), Uttar Pradesh, and is among the most sacred Shaiva shrines. Option B (Godavari) is a tempting distractor because Godavari is called the 'Ganga of the South' and is associated with Trimbakeshwar — another Jyotirlinga — leading candidates to conflate the two.

questions.stem: The Kailasa Temple at Ellora Caves, considered the world's largest monolithic rock-cut structure, was commissioned by which Rashtrakuta ruler?

options.option_text: Amoghavarsha I, a celebrated literary patron of the dynasty
Krishna I, who ruled the Rashtrakutas in the 8th century CE
Dantidurga, the acknowledged founder of the Rashtrakuta dynasty
Dhruva Dharavarsha, who defeated the Gurjara-Pratiharas decisively

questions.explanation: Kailasa Temple (Cave 16) was commissioned by Rashtrakuta king Krishna I around 756–773 CE. Option A (Amoghavarsha I) is the most dangerous distractor — he is the dynasty's most celebrated ruler, famous for literary patronage of Kannada literature — but he ruled nearly a century after the temple was carved and is not associated with Kailasa's construction.

questions.stem: The Lepakshi Temple in Andhra Pradesh, famous for its 'hanging pillar' that appears to float above the ground, is primarily dedicated to which deity?

options.option_text: Lord Virupaksha, the presiding deity of Hampi's main temple
Lord Veerabhadra, a fierce and powerful form of Lord Shiva
Lord Vishnu in his Venkateswara form worshipped at Tirupati
Lord Subramanya, the son of Lord Shiva and Goddess Parvati

questions.explanation: Lepakshi Temple (formally Veerabhadra Temple) in Anantapur district, Andhra Pradesh, is dedicated to Veerabhadra — a fierce emanation of Shiva — and was built during the Vijayanagara period (16th century). Option A (Virupaksha) is a classic trap: Virupaksha is another Shaiva deity whose famous temple is at nearby Hampi, causing candidates to conflate the two Vijayanagara-era Shaiva sites.

questions.stem: The Konark Sun Temple in Odisha — a UNESCO World Heritage Site — was constructed by which ruler of the Eastern Ganga dynasty?

options.option_text: Narasimhadeva I, an Eastern Ganga ruler of the 13th century
Anantavarman Chodaganga, builder of the Jagannath Temple Puri
Kapilendra Deva, the founder of the Gajapati dynasty in Odisha
Prataparudra Deva, considered the last great Gajapati ruler

questions.explanation: Konark Sun Temple was built by Narasimhadeva I of the Eastern Ganga dynasty around 1250 CE. Option B (Anantavarman Chodaganga) is the strongest distractor — he is the most famous Eastern Ganga ruler, credited with commissioning the Jagannath Temple at Puri — and candidates frequently transfer his patronage to Konark. Options C and D belonged to the later Gajapati dynasty, a separate lineage.

questions.stem: The Brihadeeswara Temple at Gangaikonda Cholapuram — lesser-known than its Thanjavur twin — was built by which Chola emperor to commemorate a northward military triumph?

options.option_text: Rajaraja Chola I, the builder of the famous Thanjavur Brihadeeswara
Kulottunga Chola I, who united the Eastern Chalukya-Chola lineages
Rajendra Chola I, who led campaigns all the way to the river Ganga
Vikrama Chola, renowned as a major patron of Shaiva temples

questions.explanation: Gangaikonda Cholapuram ('city of the Chola who took the Ganga') was founded by Rajendra Chola I after his successful campaigns reaching the Gangetic plain; he built its Brihadeeswara Temple around 1035 CE. Option A (Rajaraja Chola I) is the most dangerous distractor — candidates know he built the Thanjavur Brihadeeswara and instinctively assign this near-identical temple to the same ruler, overlooking that it was his son Rajendra's monument to a different conquest.

questions.stem: The Ambubachi Mela, one of India's largest tantric gatherings held annually at Kamakhya Temple in Assam, primarily commemorates which belief associated with the goddess?

options.option_text: The annual flooding of the Brahmaputra as a sign of the goddess's grace
The annual menstrual cycle of Goddess Kamakhya, a core Shakti Peetha belief
The goddess's annual descent from the Nilachal Hill to bless all devotees
The celestial marriage of Goddess Kamakhya with Lord Shiva on Nilachal Hill

questions.explanation: Ambubachi Mela at Kamakhya Temple (Nilachal Hill, Guwahati) is rooted in the tantric belief that the earth goddess undergoes her annual menstruation (rajaswala). The temple is sealed for three days, then reopens for the festival — a practice unique among major Indian temples. Option D (marriage of Kamakhya) is drawn from confusion with Madurai's Meenakshi Thirukalyanam; Option A conflates unrelated Brahmaputra flood folklore with the temple's actual ritual tradition.
